mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If destination state is a Hague Apostille Convention party, notarize the Certificate in New Zealand and obtain a single apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; if destination state is not a Hague party, notarize the Certificate and complete New Zealand MFAT authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand; never add apostille to consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Status Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If destination state is a Hague Apostille Convention party, obtain the status certificate from the Companies Office, notarize it, and apostillize it through the Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; if destination state is not a Hague party, notarize and process solely through MFAT authentication and destination consular legalization; the two paths are parallel and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the New Zealand limited company, countersigned by the company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If destination state is a Hague party, execute before a New Zealand notary public and obtain a single apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs; if destination state is not a Hague party, execute before a New Zealand notary public and complete MFAT authentication and destination consular legalization only; no apostille may be added after consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand limited company through its shareholders and directors as filed with the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague destination, have the certified copy notarized and apostilled by the Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; for non-Hague destination, have the certified copy notarized and carry out MFAT authentication plus consular legalization at the destination diplomatic mission in New Zealand; never combine apostille and consular legalization in one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand registered bank (e.g., ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited, Bank of New Zealand, ASB Bank Limited, or Westpac New Zealand Limited)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the reference letter on bank letterhead with a banker's wet signature; if the destination is a Hague state, notarize the banker's signature and apostillize via the Department of Internal Affairs; if the destination is a non-Hague state, notarize the banker's signature and complete MFAT authentication and consular legalization at the destination consulate; no apostille is to be added to the consular legalization path.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every beneficial owner, director, officer, signatory and shareholder at or above the 25% threshold must be screened before onboarding against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the New Zealand targeted financial sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and its associated regulations, the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the UK HM Treasury sanctions list. The AML/CFT programme must record the screening algorithm, false-positive disposition, and review cadence. PEP screening covers foreign and domestic PEPs, immediate family members, close associates, and high-risk sectors; enhanced due diligence is mandated for all retail securities brokerage counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register online portal operated by the New Zealand Companies Office (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use English or Maori in Latin script; the registry normalizes macronated Maori vowels for collision comparison. The proposed name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing registered, reserved or alternate name. The four-tier naming hierarchy is: (1) exact reserved or registered company name; (2) name of an overseas company registered in New Zealand; (3) an approved alternative name; and (4) phonetically transliterated foreign-script name supported by a certified English transliteration declaration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of receiving a name rejection, the applicant must file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies at the New Zealand Companies Office, stating the statutory ground challenged and attaching any ministerial or regulator consent required for sensitive tokens. If the objection is identity or substantial similarity, the applicant may submit a signed letter of consent from the existing name holder or an undertaking to change that name. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the review provisions of the Companies Act 1993, serving the Registrar and instructing New Zealand counsel within the applicable statutory time limit. Simultaneously, the applicant may file a fresh reservation with a distinctive prefix or sector descriptor.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand and open for service of process during business hours; a PO Box or commercial mailbox alone is void. A serviced virtual office with a physical street address, lease, signage and local staff can nominally satisfy the Companies Act 1993, but for ISIC 6611 retail securities brokerage the Financial Markets Authority, Inland Revenue and NZ banks will reject a pure virtual-mailbox model because the place of effective management and client trust-account custody must be demonstrable in New Zealand. The brokerage must maintain substantive premises, local directors and staff, and auditable records before FMA licensing or bank onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verified lease or deed; (2) physical signage; (3) real staff presence; (4) board minutes and resolutions physically kept in New Zealand; (5) client money trust account records; (6) AML/CFT procedure manual; (7) employer and tax registrations; (8) directors' declarations and UBO records. Quantified risk of unannounced inspection in the first 12 months: Inland Revenue high (80%), FMA AML/CFT on-site supervision high (90%), Companies Office registered-office verification medium (45%), and municipal commercial occupancy inspection low (15%).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, sections 12-19 (incorporation), 122-129 (constitution, issue of shares and consideration), 151-152 (directors), 184 (registered office); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Part 2 (market services licences) and Part 4 (client money and client property); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Company Incorporation Application and Form 2 Consent to Appointment as Director, together with the company constitution and registered office consent, filed online via the Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand Companies Act 1993 does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up share capital for registration of a limited company. The directors may determine the share capital and issue shares for such consideration as the board considers fair and reasonable under sections 123-127 of the Act. No blocked escrow account is required by the Companies Office for formation. Where the Financial Markets Authority imposes prudential or regulatory capital requirements on the company as a licensed derivatives issuer or financial advice provider, those requirements arise at the licensing stage and are separate from the formation capital rule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF NZ_LTD

The undersigned, being the duly appointed director(s) of NZ_LTD (the Company), acting by written resolution under the Companies Act 1993 and the Company's constitution, hereby resolve and record as follows:

1. CONSTITUTION AND REGISTRATION. The constitution appended to the Company's incorporation application is adopted as the constitution of the Company in accordance with section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. The directors are authorised to file the registration application, to pay the prescribed Companies Office fee, and to make any minor amendments to the constitution as may reasonably be required by the New Zealand Companies Office to secure registration.

2. SHARE CAPITAL AND ALLOTMENT. The Company's authorised share capital is established as such number of ordinary shares, with such nominal value, as is stated in the incorporation application. The initial shares are allotted to the subscribers named in the application at a consideration determined by the directors in accordance with sections 123-127 of the Companies Act 1993. The consideration may be satisfied in cash, property, or services, and the shares may be issued as fully paid or partly paid as the board decides. The board confirms that no statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for formation and that no escrow account is required by the Companies Office.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the street address set out in the incorporation application, being a physical address in New Zealand, and the directors are authorised to file the registered office notice under section 184 of the Companies Act 1993. The registered office shall be open for service of documents during ordinary business hours and shall be the address at which the Company's statutory registers are kept.

4. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS. The persons named in the consent forms are appointed as directors of the Company. Each director has consented to act and has provided the required statutory declarations and identity documents. If applicable, the board appoints the person named in the resolution as company secretary, not being required unless the board determines otherwise. All directors shall exercise their powers and duties in good faith and with the care, diligence, and skill required by the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

5. BANKING MANDATE. The directors are authorised to open and maintain bank accounts with the Company's chosen bank, including a general operating account and a segregated client money account if required by the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. The bank mandate shall require the signatures of any two directors, or such other signatories and limits as the board determines, and the directors are authorised to provide specimen signatures, corporate authorisations, and any bank forms required.

6. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND ACCOUNTING. The financial year of the Company is fixed to end on 31 March. The directors shall ensure that financial records, the share register, the director register, and the register of charges are maintained and available for inspection as required by law. Board meetings may be held by telephone, videoconference, or other electronic means provided that all participating directors can communicate with each other.

7. REGULATORY AUTHORISATIONS. The directors are authorised to prepare and lodge all applications and registrations necessary for the Company's offshore securities brokerage business, including Financial Service Providers Register registration, Financial Markets Authority market services licensing, AML/CFT registration, tax registration with Inland Revenue, and any local authority or Fire and Emergency New Zealand approvals. The directors are authorised to appoint professional advisers and to pay all related fees.

8. GENERAL AUTHORITY. The Company may execute leases, engagement letters, compliance manuals, client agreements, insurance policies, and such other contracts as are reasonably necessary to commence business. Certified copies of this resolution shall be provided to bankers, regulators, auditors, and professional advisers on request. This resolution takes effect upon the registration of the Company and may be referred to as the First Board Resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Name Reservation and Pre-Filing Compliance Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal (RealMe authenticated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the New Zealand Companies Register using the RealMe login. The proposed company name must not be identical to an existing or reserved name, must not contain restricted words such as "bank", "trust", or "exchange" without Financial Markets Authority or Reserve Bank of New Zealand clearance, and must not be offensive or misleading. Reserve the name online if the Companies Office requires it. For offshore shareholders or non-resident directors, prepare notarized copies of passports, proof of residential address, and signed consent to act as director; if any document is in a foreign language, arrange a certified English translation. Ensure that all diplomatic legalisation or Hague Apostille formalities are completed in the country of origin because the Companies Office and banks may require certified evidence of identity and authority. Retain the name search reference for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name search reference or reservation confirmation
Notarized passport copy of each proposed director and shareholder
Proof of residential address for each director (notarized, not more than 3 months old)
Certified English translation of any non-English document
Power of attorney or board authorisation for any corporate shareholder or overseas agent
AML/CFT pre-incorporation business records, if required by bank or FMA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the name as prohibited or misleadingly similar, respond within 12 working days by selecting an alternate name or by obtaining the required regulatory consent from FMA or the Reserve Bank. If documents are queried for notarisation issues, provide a fully notarised replacement or an apostilled version and re-upload the corrected record through the Companies Office response facility.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the online Company Incorporation Application and Consent to Appointment as Director forms through the Companies Register. Include the constitution, the registered office street address in New Zealand which must not be a post office box, the principal place of business address, the share structure, and the initial allotment of shares as approved by the board resolution. Ensure that at least one director is a natural person resident in New Zealand or Australia, as required by the Companies Act 1993, unless an applicable exception or approved nominee director is used. Pay the prescribed filing fee by credit card or online banking. On successful registration, the Companies Office will issue a New Zealand Business Number and an electronic Certificate of Incorporation. Verify all legal entity details, retrieve the certificate from the Companies Register, and retain the certificate along with the stamped constitution and consent forms as the definitive corporate record.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Company Incorporation Application or equivalent online application
Form 2 Consent to Appointment as Director for each appointed director
Constitution of the Company signed by the subscribers
Consent of the occupier for each registered office and principal place of business address
Share allotment application and the First Board Resolution
Prescribed filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office suspends or queries the application, use the Companies Register correction workflow to amend the defective fields and resubmit within the stated deadline. If a director consent is rejected because of residency, address, or qualification issues, replace or add a compliant New Zealand or Australian resident director and file a fresh Form 2. If the certificate is not issued within the SLA, contact the Companies Office contact centre with the application reference number and escalate to the Registrar if no resolution is given within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue and CRS/FATCA Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (New Zealand), MyIR online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company with Inland Revenue using the New Zealand Business Number. Apply for the company's IRD number and determine whether GST registration is required or voluntary; registration is compulsory if taxable supplies exceed the GST threshold of NZD 60,000 per twelve-month period. Register for PAYE if the company will employ staff in New Zealand, and consider dividend withholding payment and resident withholding tax obligations if distributions will be made to shareholders. Because the business is an offshore securities brokerage, assess whether the company qualifies as an investment entity for Common Reporting Standard and FATCA registration, and if so, register with Inland Revenue as a reporting financial institution and complete the applicable IRD entity information questionnaires. Maintain documentary evidence of all tax registrations and appoint a New Zealand tax agent if the board wishes to delegate compliance administration.
required_dossiers: NZBN and Certificate of Incorporation
Bank account details or statutory declaration for IRD purposes
GST registration questionnaire if applicable
PAYE employer registration form if applicable
CRS/FATCA financial institution registration questionnaire if applicable
Board resolution appointing any tax agent or authorised representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the IRD number or GST application, respond to the notice in MyIR within the stated due date and provide the requested business activity evidence. If there is a delay in CRS/FATCA registration, request a confirmation of the entity classification from Inland Revenue and, if necessary, appoint a specialist tax adviser to correct the questionnaire. Any late registration charge can be mitigated by showing the appropriate date of incorporation and registration evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Services Licensing, FSPR Registration and AML/CFT Programme Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the company's offshore securities brokerage activities require registration on the Financial Service Providers Register under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and whether the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 requires a market services licence for derivatives issuer, financial advice provider, or managed investment scheme activities. Prepare a full application through the FMA licensing portal, including a detailed business plan, conflict of interest management arrangements, complaints handling and internal dispute resolution framework, AML/CFT compliance programme under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, proposed outsourcing and supervision arrangements, financial capacity and regulatory capital evidence, and client money handling rules if client money will be held. Join an approved financial dispute resolution scheme. If the company will issue CFDs or other derivatives to retail clients, the FMA will assess treatment of clients, fair dealing, and margin lending practices. If the activity is entirely offshore with no New Zealand nexus, document the applicable exclusion or exemption and seek a written legal opinion before relying on it.
required_dossiers: FSPR online registration application
FMA market services licence application (if applicable)
AML/CFT compliance programme and business risk assessment
Business plan, budget and regulatory capital statement
Complaints handling procedure and approved dispute resolution scheme enrolment
Conflict of interest and inducement management policy
Client money and client asset handling arrangement, if applicable
Personal history and fit and proper information for directors and senior managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA issues a request for further information or a notice of deficient application, respond within the deadline with a complete supplementary pack. If the licence is refused, the board may apply to the FMA for reconsideration, submit a materially revised application, or seek judicial review in the High Court. In parallel, the company must not commence regulated financial services until the FMA licence and FSPR registration are effective. Where the FSPR application is suspended, rectify any errors in the online record and confirm continuing membership of an approved dispute resolution scheme.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance for Operational Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority (city or district council), Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and WorkSafe New Zealand (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company occupies physical office premises in New Zealand, secure a building warrant of fitness from the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004 before staff or client-facing operations begin. The warrant certifies that the building compliance schedule is current and that all specified systems, including emergency lighting, fire alarms, and escape routes, have been inspected and maintained. If the premises is a commercial office, submit a fire evacuation scheme for approval by Fire and Emergency New Zealand if required by the risk profile, and conduct the required yearly evacuation drills. Implement a health and safety policy, hazard register, first aid arrangements, and worker engagement system under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. For a purely virtual or digital back-office operation with no physical occupancy, record the principal place of business address and note that no industrial process, environmental permit, or hazardous materials licence applies. The company must also comply with electricity and computer room fire safety obligations if it operates any private server or equipment room.
required_dossiers: Building warrant of fitness and compliance schedule issued by the territorial authority
Fire evacuation scheme approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand, if applicable
Health and safety policy and risk register
Lease agreement or occupancy certificate for the registered office
Professional indemnity and public liability insurance certificates
First aid assessment, equipment inspection records and emergency contact roster
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the territorial authority refuses to issue a building warrant of fitness, rectify the compliance schedule deficiencies and request a re-inspection. If the fire evacuation scheme is rejected by Fire and Emergency New Zealand, amend the plan to reflect the building occupancy, egress, and alarm activation requirements and resubmit. Where WorkSafe identifies a health and safety deficiency, issue an improvement plan, undertake internal corrective action, and confirm compliance within the timeframe of any notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: In lieu of an industrial licensing board, the statutory regulatory authority is the Financial Markets Authority (FMA), New Zealand, together with the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR). For any physical premises, the local territorial authority and Fire and Emergency New Zealand are the relevant operational safety authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: FMA Market Services Licence under Part 2 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (derivatives issuer / financial advice provider as applicable); Financial Service Providers Register registration; approved dispute resolution scheme membership; AML/CFT registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — no industrial process, manufacturing, chemical operation, assembly or warehousing activity is carried out under ISIC 6611. Where a commercial office is occupied, the relevant authority is the local territorial authority under the Building Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no Environmental Impact Assessment required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation is associated with offshore securities brokerage or retail agency for equities, CFDs and derivative instruments. Office waste, if any, is handled through municipal collection services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not an industrial civil defence permit threshold. For leased commercial premises, obtain a current building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004, any fire evacuation scheme approval required by Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and a compliant workplace health and safety framework under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. No civil defence fire permit is required absent a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing process. For a virtual office with no physical operations, the requirement is Not Applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand Limited Company (NZ Ltd), the entity must first obtain an IRD number (tax file number) by submitting the IR596 form (Company Registration) either online via myIR or through the Companies Office joint registration process. The application requires the Certificate of Incorporation, details of all directors and shareholders (including non-resident beneficial owners), and a description of the intended business activities. Once the IRD number is issued, the company must assess its GST obligations. If the company expects to make taxable supplies exceeding NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, it must register for GST using the IR356 form (GST Registration) or via myIR. For non-resident directors or shareholders, additional identification and proof of address may be required. The company must also register for PAYE (Pay As You Earn) if it employs staff, and for FBT (Fringe Benefit Tax) if applicable. All registrations are completed through the Inland Revenue's online portal, myIR, which serves as the primary electronic filing and compliance platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Look-Through Company (LTC) election under the Income Tax Act 2007 (Subpart HB); Hybrid mismatch rules under Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007; for GST, the option to zero-rate certain supplies of financial services to non-residents under Section 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and supported via the Peppol network. GST invoices must contain prescribed particulars under Section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including supplier name and GST number, date of issue, description of goods/services, and amount of GST. Tax invoices must be issued within 28 days of the supply. Anti-fraud measures include mandatory record retention for 7 years and the requirement to file GST returns electronically via myIR. There is no digital stamping or API-based clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the supply are zero-rated. Services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and where the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand, are zero-rated. Certain financial services supplied to non-residents (including offshore securities brokerage) may be zero-rated under Section 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, provided the recipient is a non-resident and the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand. The supplier must hold sufficient evidence to substantiate the zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Bank remittance statement or foreign currency receipt
Signed contract or agreement with the non-resident recipient (for services)
Proof of non-resident status of the recipient (e.g., certificate of incorporation or tax residency certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is incorrectly claimed, the supplier is liable for GST at 15% on the supply, plus penalties and interest under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Penalties include a late payment penalty of 1% per month and a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall for intentional or reckless errors. Additionally, if goods are not exported within the required 28-day period, the supply is subject to GST and the supplier may be required to claw back any input tax credits previously claimed. Inland Revenue conducts risk-based audits on export zero-rating claims, particularly for financial services, and may require detailed documentation to verify the non-resident status of recipients and the actual provision of services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a freely floating currency with full conversion of both current and capital account transactions under a liberalised regulatory framework. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not impose exchange controls, and the New Zealand dollar is fully convertible for trade, direct investment, financial transactions, and profit remittance. There is no surrender requirement for export proceeds, no central bank approval threshold for inward or outward capital flows, and no administrative restriction on the repatriation of dividends, share capital, or liquidation proceeds. The primary regulatory constraints are not FX controls but prudential supervision, AML/CFT obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and certain screening requirements under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for foreign ownership of sensitive land or material business assets. A securities brokerage company with non-resident shareholders must document that the brokerage itself does not hold such sensitive assets, and must file accurate Balance of Payments/International Transaction Reporting System (ITRS) declarations through its settlement bank. Remittance hurdles may arise only when a bank perceives elevated ML/TF risk for a high-risk financial-services entity; in such cases, enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds evidence must be supplied. Foreign investors may hold NZD or offshore foreign-currency accounts and may hedge freely using deliverable forwards and swap markets, subject to commonly observed market documentation and credit-limit requirements. Overall, the NZ regime is categorised as no exchange control or open capital account, with compliance-focused frictions only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender regime exists under New Zealand law. Exporters retain full title to foreign currency receipts, may keep proceeds in New Zealand or offshore foreign-currency accounts, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio or timeline. All offshore receipts must merely be reported for Balance of Payments statistical purposes via the International Transactions Reporting System. The practical banking requirement is to provide the settlement bank with underlying export/transaction documentation to support the SWIFT purpose code and to facilitate transaction monitoring.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Segregated Client Money Trust Account and Operational NZD/Foreign Currency Accounts
Segregated Client Money Trust Account (Financial Markets Conduct Act 2006) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Currency Account with SWIFT GPI and Automated Settlement Integration
Institutional Transaction Banking Account and Multi-Entity Clearing Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for a licensed New Zealand retail securities broker. Fintech EMIs generally lack the segregated client money architecture mandated by the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2006 and often cannot provide acceptable independent trust attestations that satisfy New Zealand’s prudential banking expectations. The Financial Markets Authority requires licensed brokers to hold client funds in an authorised local bank on trust; unlicensed EMIs would be non-compliant for this purpose. Limited utility may exist as a payment-only rail for settlement of Visa/Mastercard flows, but the core treasury function must sit with locally incorporated registered banks. Legal constraints also include the requirement that a non-bank EMI servicing New Zealand entities must obtain a flat tax/AML/CFT registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, and may not legally operate as a deposit-taker without a banking licence. Therefore, a prudent sponsor should reject EMIs for primary liquidity and use them, if at all, exclusively for sub-ordinated disbursement channels with strict transaction caps.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is typically mandatory for at least one statutory director of the high-risk brokerage when opening the segregated client money account. Most Tier 1 banks require a formal in-branch interview with certified identification, originals or notarised copies of corporate registry filings, and a compliance committee presentation of the business model. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted in narrow cases only where the director appears before a New Zealand diplomatic post or a consular officer recognised by the bank, followed by a video interview with life-event verification. Even then, the bank retains discretion to require the company secretary and local counsel to attend in-branch. The practical position is that physical presence is highly recommended for at least one senior manager or a person with independent signatory authority, while non-resident directors may satisfy KYC via a combination of apostilled certifications and bank-to-bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification under ISIC 6611 creates an automatic enhanced-risk profile, particularly when offering CFDs and derivatives to non-resident retail clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified Financial Markets Authority (FMA) Derivatives Issuer Licence, current AML/CFT risk assessment prepared under the Terrorism Financing Act, client money segregation audit certificate, a copy of the regulatory compliance manual with transaction monitoring thresholds, and a Board resolution adopting the full KYC program.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership chain with layered companies and discretionary trusts obscuring ultimate economic interest, triggering a bank's refusal to onboard without fully transparent beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full New Zealand Companies Office extract, complete corporate chart, trust deed and registered trust-information return, source of wealth declarations for every natural person holding greater than 25% of the entity, plus a licensed New Zealand legal opinion confirming the unbroken chain of control and economic exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or client payment flows originating from jurisdictions with stringent FX controls or high money-laundering risk, potentially causing unwelcome scrutiny under sanctions and PEP filters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and Politically Exposed Persons screening certificates for all connected parties, original trade/contract documentation for each pay-in, correspondent-bank confirmation of FX purpose codes, transaction-level audit trail of the brokerage execution systems, and a dedicated compliance officer attestation that source-of-funds files are retrievable within 48 hours.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection from non-operating revenue or unexplained third-party deposits, potentially suggesting capital laundering or unlicensed deposit-taking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chartered accountant independent verification of provenance, audited brokerage business plan with six-quarter revenue and liquidity projections, proof of tax residency and tax payment registrations for all ultimate shareholders, and the FMA approval letter specifically authorising the securities brokerage licence. The directors must also produce bank statements of the sending external accounts for at least twelve months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection must be structured via a SWIFT MT103/MT202 wire using the explicit instruction 'equity contribution to NZ Limited for capitalisation', with an economic purpose code matching the incoming capital transfer under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's International Transactions Reporting System. The receiving bank will issue a foreign investment inflow declaration, and capital verification is completed after settlement through a statutory auditor's certificate to the effect that the funds have been credited to the NZD capital escrow account. No central bank pre-approval is required, but the bank will require the underlying legal agreement, shareholder resolution, and evidence of overseas banking source in order to apply the appropriate balance-of-payments classification. The final capital verification should also include an audit trail linking the capital account on the Companies Office register to the exact foreign inward funds, including all currency conversion confirmation tickets.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for open-account payments, with all outgoing messages carrying full counterparty identifiers and accurate purpose codes. Commercial letters of credit issued by the settlement bank under UCP 600 are recommended for high-value physical commodity settlements or where the counterparty requires a bank guarantee. Documentary collections under URC 522 are acceptable for medium-trust relationships where underlying transport documents provide shielding. Client money disbursements to offshore brokers or liquidity providers must be separately tracked through a segregated client money account using SWIFT GPI with strict beneficiary verification, and must not be combined with proprietary capital. All outgoing transfers require the underlying trade agreement, invoice, FX transaction ticket, and beneficial-ownership confirmation, with records retained for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts for NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/AUD, and NZD/JPY with maturities up to 24 months, provided they are booked under an ISDA or active own-funds collateral arrangement with a licensed New Zealand bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or offshore currencies such as CNY, INR, and IDR, only where the underlying exposure is a genuine commercial trade settlement and the NDF is transacted through a permitted Tier 1 bank or an authorised derivatives dealer.

Cross-currency swaps solely for the purpose of aligning long-term foreign currency assets with foreign currency liabilities arising from client segregation trust balances, subject to FMA conduct guidance and board-approved treasury policies.

Foreign exchange options used to hedge contingent brokerage settlement exposures, limited to cash-settled contracts with maximum maturity of twelve months and closed-out before any speculative use of client funds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Company under section 208 of the Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date; the annual return date is the anniversary of incorporation, or the six-month anniversary of the adopted balance date where a balance date has been set, such as 30 September for a 31 March balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$50.00 plus continued monthly late filing penalty until the return is delivered; failure to file for more than six months after the annual return date allows the Registrar to issue a 10-working-day removal notice and strike the company off the New Zealand register under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993, with all company property vesting in the Crown

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FMC reporting entity financial statements and independent auditor's report under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office; copy filed on the Financial Markets Authority disclosure register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the balance date for an FMC reporting entity; a large non-FMC company must file within 5 months after the balance date; the statements must be signed and dated by the directors before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; directors may be liable for civil penalties and infringement fees up to NZ$100,000 for a body corporate, with continued default capable of leading to FMA enforcement, director banning, and strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Service Providers Register annual confirmation, update of particulars, and levy payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority as Registrar of Financial Service Providers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of the entity's FSP registration; any change to addresses, principal officer, directors, complainant handling process, dispute resolution scheme, or regulated services must be lodged within 20 working days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm and update the FSP registration may result in cancellation by the Financial Markets Authority; providing financial services without current registration is an offence under the Financial Service Providers Act 2008 carrying fines up to NZ$100,000 for a body corporate, and the securities brokerage license would be forfeited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT annual compliance report and associated beneficial ownership and compliance program update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority as the AML/CFT supervisor for securities and derivatives brokerage; suspicious transaction reports are filed with the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the reporting entity's financial year; the AML/CFT compliance program, risk assessment, and customer due diligence records must be updated annually and kept at the New Zealand registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 exposes the body corporate to civil pecuniary penalties up to NZ$2,000,000 and the FMA may suspend, restrict, or revoke the entity's participation in the financial markets if the annual report is not delivered

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and services tax return and payment where the brokerage is GST-registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the 28th day of the month following the end of each monthly or two-monthly taxable period; if the annual GST filing basis is approved, payment is due no later than the 28th day of the sixth month after the balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inland Revenue late filing penalties escalate from NZ$50 for the first late return to NZ$250, NZ$500, and NZ$1,000 for repeated late returns; use-of-money interest applies to unpaid GST and continued non-compliance may trigger default assessments and civil debt enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer monthly schedule and PAYE/KiwiSaver deduction payment where the brokerage employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the employee payments and PAYE deductions were made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid PAYE is treated as a trust debt owed to the Crown; IRD late filing and late payment penalties apply, directors may become personally liable for PAYE and KiwiSaver deductions, and persistent default can lead to wind-up proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and corporate secretarial maintenance of the share register, director register, charges register, and minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; the registers and minute book must be available at the registered office or registered agent in New Zealand for inspection by shareholders, directors, and the Registrar on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; an internal annual audit should be completed in conjunction with the annual return date, and all changes to directors, shareholders, registered office, and charges must be filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain statutory registers or minute books is an offence under section 368 of the Companies Act 1993 with fines up to NZ$10,000 for the company and every defaulting director; inaccurate registers may invalidate share transfers and expose the company to misfeasance claims

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified audit is compulsory if: (1) the entity is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, which includes a licensed derivatives issuer or a market services licensee providing retail equities, CFD, and derivative brokerage services, regardless of asset, revenue, or employee size; (2) the entity is a large company under section 45 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013, meaning total assets at balance date exceed NZ$60,000,000, total revenue for the accounting period exceeds NZ$30,000,000, or the company has 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; (3) shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares exercise their statutory right to require an audit; or (4) the AML/CFT supervisor requires an independent compliance audit of the brokerage's anti-money laundering program. The auditor must be a chartered accountant licensed to act as auditor in New Zealand and must comply with the External Reporting Board audit and assurance standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must comply with New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice as set by the External Reporting Board. FMC reporting entities and large companies must use Tier 1 New Zealand equivalents to IFRS unless eligible for Tier 2 NZ IFRS with reduced disclosure under the XRB Accounting Standards Framework; small non-FMC entities may apply the simplified Tier 3 or Tier 4 standards where eligible, but a retail securities brokerage holding an FMC market services license will ordinarily be required to present Tier 1 NZ IFRS financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a public UBO register, and the Companies Office annual return does not require a beneficial ownership schedule. The entity must instead maintain a complete register of members, record every share transfer in the register of members promptly and no later than 30 days after presentation of a valid transfer, file a notice of share issue with the Companies Office within 20 working days when new shares are issued, and file any constitutional or share capital change within 20 working days. As a licensed financial entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the brokerage must identify and verify every beneficial owner before establishing a business relationship, perform enhanced due diligence for high-risk offshore clients, re-verify beneficial ownership at intervals commensurate with risk, and include the beneficial ownership refresh results in the annual AML/CFT compliance report. Any change of beneficial ownership that has no legitimate explanation must be considered for reporting as a suspicious transaction to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of board and shareholder meetings
Register of AML/CFT customer due diligence and beneficial ownership records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 2,500 per annum depending on city, registered office service, and corporate secretarial package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 35,000 per annum for a Tier 1 NZ IFRS statutory audit of a small or medium securities brokerage, plus USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 if a separate AML/CFT compliance audit is required by the Financial Markets Authority

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays; R&D tax credit 20% (12.5% for SME R&D under certain conditions) and 150% innovation intensity credit for eligible R&D; reduced effective rates available through legitimate tax deductions (e.g., depreciation on commercial property and certain eligible fixed assets). Preferential regime available for approved PIE (portfolio investment entity) income only where applicable, not for a standard securities brokerage.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or as part of approved electronic filing provider systems (e.g., tax agents using IRD File or commercial software).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For standard 31 March balance dates, filing is due by 7 July of the same calendar year. For non-standard balance dates, the return is due by the 7th day of the month that corresponds with the end of the company's 12-month accounting period. Certain tax agents may obtain extensions to 31 March of the following year or another extended date per IRD practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from all sources, including commissions, spreads, CFD/equity brokerage fees, margin lending interest, and other trading income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: New Zealand-sourced income only is taxable unless the company is resident; residence is governed by incorporation and centre of management rules. Non-resident companies with a New Zealand PE are taxable on PE-attributable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: brokerage clearing fees, infrastructure, staff costs, regulatory fees, interest expense, and other ordinary business deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced income; branch-specific allocations should be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3: Net Taxable Income / Tax Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions offset by tax losses brought forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents carrying on business through a PE may offset PE losses against PE profits subject to continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RWT, foreign tax credits, and imputation credits claimed to reduce corporate tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed under NZ DTA provisions only if non-resident company is subject to NZ tax on the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final core tax at 28% after deducting credits and provisional tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no PE exists, no income tax return is needed and the company only remains subject to NRWT/AIL on New Zealand-source dividends, interest, and royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 for the first month and another NZD 250 after one month of continued non-filing (maximum NZD 500 for non-individuals). Late payment penalty applies at 1% immediately and 4% per six-month period on unpaid tax, plus accruing interest on unpaid tax at the IRD prescribed rate (currently 8.38% per annum).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on gross dividends; 15% NRWT for fully imputed dividends paid to non-residents; 15% AIL if elected for certain public or marketable securities. Non-resident companies cannot access imputation credits personally.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty withholding rate: (1) obtain a certificate of residence from the foreign jurisdiction; (2) provide NZ payer with a completed resident withholding tax exemption certificate (IR451) or the relevant declaration; (3) submit a claim for refund if excess was withheld; (4) for AIL, register with IRD as an Approved Issuer and pay AIL at 2% of gross interest (where applicable) instead of NRWT; (5) treaty claims are subject to limitation-of-benefits and beneficial ownership clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest and royalties is 15%. Under DTAs, rates often reduced: interest 10-15% (e.g., Australia and US treaties 10%); royalties typically 10-15% (e.g., Australia 10%, US 10% for certain industrial royalties). If AIL is used on eligible interest, 2% AIL applies. No withholding on offshore brokerage fees unless they constitute royalties or management fees sourced in NZ.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1 million for cross-border related-party transactions requiring basic contemporaneous documentation; NZD 10 million for high-value transactions requiring robust Master File/Local File-style documentation; tax avoidance reassessment and penalties can apply below these thresholds where the arrangement lacks commercial substance.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have a separate ESR bureau; however, the Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act incorporate arm's length provisions (Part GC) and GAAR (s BG 1) that require substance over form. A brokerage incorporated in New Zealand but managed and controlled offshore may be treated as non-resident under s YD 2, but if managed in NZ or purposely structured to avoid tax, income can be re-attributed; the CFC and FIF regimes also disregard artificial structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying brokerage records, underreporting customer trades, or concealing New Zealand-sourced income in offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 150% of tax shortfall plus criminal fines up to NZD 250,000 for a company; imprisonment up to 5 years under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143A (evasion).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly concerned in evasion can be personally prosecuted and fined up to NZD 50,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years; civil action also allows recovery of unpaid tax from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an offshore brokerage conduit with no employees, no local board oversight, and no independent trading capability solely to arbitrage tax treaties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR cancellation of tax advantages (s BG 1); reassessment as agent or PE of offshore principal; penalties for abusive tax position up to 100% of tax avoided; Companies Office action for insolvent or misuse of company structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of shell companies may be personally liable for debts under Companies Act 1993 s 300 (reckless trading), disqualified for up to 5 years, and subjected to civil recovery orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as a reporting entity or implement risk-based customer due diligence for clients using wire transfers and card rails; omitting suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to NZD 2 million per breach for a reporting entity; criminal fines up to NZD 200,000 for individuals; revocation of financial services or broking licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers may be liable personally for knowing participation; imprisonment up to 2 years; travel bans can be imposed while investigations are ongoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing broking or derivative dealing services to retail clients without a Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 license from the Financial Markets Authority, or acting outside registered financial service provider scope.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to NZD 1 million; statutory damages; confiscation of profits; client transaction voidability; mandatory compensation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals directly engaged in unlicensed conduct face fines up to NZD 300,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years, plus unlimited civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Transfer Pricing Documentation Defaults
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-filing of IR4, non-preparation of transfer pricing documentation for related-party brokerage fees, or material false declarations regarding cross-border service allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalties up to NZD 500 per return; shortfall penalties from 20% to 150% depending on culpability; TP adjustment to raise taxable income and interest accruals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or tolerate transfer pricing manipulation can be made jointly and severally liable for corporate tax amounts under tax administration and general compensatory principles.
